newsitem.title: USA: Tatham Offshore granted royalty relief.
newsitem.headline: Tatham Offshore granted royalty relief.

text.p: Tatham Offshore said Friday U.S. regulators waived royalties on the first 52.5 million barrels of oil equivalent from its Sunday Silence deepwater project in Gulf of Mexico.
Based on $20 a barrel oil prices, abatement of the customary 12.5 percent royalty rate could be worth an estimated $130 million to the independent oil and natural gas company, a spokesman said.
"At $20 (a barrel) oil, that would be worth about $130 million to the company," spokesman Dennis Kunetka said.
The application for deepwater royalty relief was the first to be approved by the U.S. Minerals Management Service under a federal law waiving royalties to spur deepwater production, the company said.
The Sunday Silence field is located in Ewing Bank Blocks 958 and 1003 in federal waters about 1,500 feet deep off the coast of Louisiana, the company said.

A discovery well was drilled in Ewing Bank 958 in 1994, and a delineation well in Ewing Bank 1003 tested at a rate of about 8,700 barrels of oil and 5.4 million cubic feet of gas per day, the company said.
Tatham Offshore owns a 100 percent working interest in the field.
DeepTech International Inc owns about 37 percent of Tatham Offshore, the company said.
